newsitem.title: UK: London silver tests higher ground, PGMs languish.
newsitem.headline: London silver tests higher ground, PGMs languish.

text.p: Precious metals markets diverged on Tuesday as silver tested the upside, gold range-traded and the platinum group metals (PGMs) languished near recent lows.
Gold was fixed slightly firmer at $342.15 an ounce, compared with $341.40 in the morning, after getting a slight boost from silver's New York-led surge, traders said.
But prices were still lodged in a narrow $342.30-$341.25 range, and dealers saw little scope for more near-term activity.
"The market's done virtually nothing this afternoon, except for a little fund buying in New York taking silver to the top end of its range," a dealer said.
Silver ticked up to a high of $4.82, from Monday's London close of $4.71/4.73.
But prices settled back to $4.79/4.81 without hitting the top end of the $4.70-$4.85 range.
Activity in precious metals was expected to pick up in the latter part of the week after Tuesday's conclusion of the Financial Times Gold Conference in Prague.
Platinum and palladium softened early in the day on a fresh Russian statement on long-delayed PGM exports.
Yuri Kotlyar, first deputy chief executive of major PGM producer Norilsk Nickel, was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying exports would resume later this month.
A Norilsk spokesman later said the company was producing about 70 percent of the amount of PGM concentrates is did during its peak in 1989-1990. But he did not give production volumes.

In other Russian news, Finance Ministry official Vladimir Rybkin said Russia would not fully liberalise its gold market before mid-1998 and had no plans to open up its platinum metals market in the future.
Russia produces some 60 percent of the world's palladium and 20 percent of its platinum.
But after an early price drop, which took the PGMs to the lowest level in two weeks, the market stabilised and prices marked time in the afternoon.
Platinum was last quoted $10 lower at $416.00/421.00, and serious technical support was not seen until prices tested the $400 mark, dealers said.
Palladium was off $4 at $197.00/202.00. The market was still very tight, with one-month lease rates still over 100 percent, dealers said.
